# Skills demonstrated in context

A technology list alone says little about the level of a skill or how it was used. This page therefore links methods and technologies to concrete work. The contexts differ in date, depth, and evidence; the list does not imply equal or current expertise in every item.

## Applied mathematics and scientific modelling

**Context:** thesis and research on environmental transport, atmospheric dispersion, and reduced-complexity models; subsequent work on urban hydrological modelling.

- Applied mathematics and partial differential equations
- Numerical simulation and reduced-order modelling
- Fluid mechanics, atmospheric dispersion, and environmental processes
- Scientific reasoning: assumptions, model identification, approximation, and interpretation
- Fortran and SURFEX–TEB

**Evidence:** [2006 reduced-complexity modelling paper](https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/mecanique/articles/10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007/), [2008 dispersion chapter](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5_14), and the [2018 TEB-Veg hydrological-modelling paper](https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/11/4175/2018/). For model context, see the [CNRM TEB overview](https://cnrm.sedoo.fr/teb-town-energy-balance/) and [SURFEX overview](https://cnrm.sedoo.fr/surfex-2/).

## Statistics, Data Science, and machine learning

**Context:** five years of Data Science work in the Qlik/Talend lab.

- Data analysis and statistical reasoning
- Classical machine learning
- Experiment design, model comparison, and benchmark evaluation
- Classification metrics, threshold analysis, and error analysis
- Python development and industrialisation

**Evidence:** the [industrial LLM-evaluation case study](projects/llm-hallucination-evaluation.qmd) documents the evaluation methodology at a disclosure-safe level. Specific methods should be assessed against project-level evidence rather than inferred from the job-family label alone.

## LLMs, NLP, and generative AI

**Context:** industrial experimentation and evaluation of methods for detecting unsupported or hallucinated model outputs.

- State-of-the-art review and definition of an evaluation scope
- Independent evaluation pipeline and benchmark design
- Fact-checking and LLM-evaluation approaches
- Metric calculation and aggregation, threshold trade-offs, and error analysis
- Amazon Bedrock and Python-based evaluation tooling

**Evidence and limits:** the [industrial case study](projects/llm-hallucination-evaluation.qmd) describes the work without exposing private code, internal data, implementation-specific architecture, or aggregate numerical results. Qlik/Talend has not authorised disclosure of those numerical results.

## Software engineering and product development

**Context:** applied across research, startup/product development, ESN consulting, and enterprise software.

- Python — Data Science, evaluation tooling, and public software
- Java and Spring Boot — enterprise/backend application context
- Scala — enterprise software context
- JavaScript and ActionScript — application/front-end context
- PHP and front-end development
- BPM / business-process workflows
- AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker, and Kubernetes — cloud and AI-platform context
- Software design, modularity, testing, integration, and maintainability

**Public implementation evidence:** [Wiki Knowledge](https://github.com/JM-Brun/wiki-knowledge), a Python package for source ingestion, structured knowledge organisation, validation, and lexical search. Its current vector-search path falls back to BM25; it is not yet embedding-based semantic retrieval.

## Adapting across environments

The experience spans research laboratories, startup/product development, ESN consulting, and software-vendor contexts. The common skill is adapting methods and implementation choices to different constraints: scientific validity, user needs, system integration, maintainability, and operational delivery.

For the full chronology and official role titles, see [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/brunjm/).
